title: Speaker Johnson walks back talk about potentially leaving Congress
description: He said he intends to remain the House Republican leader even if his party loses the chamber.

title: New White House press secretary begins her term
description: Katie Zacharia is scheduled to hold her first briefing Tuesday.

title: Judge blocks Trump administration from airing taxpayer-funded campaign-style ads
description: A coalition of nonprofits had sued, calling the ads “propaganda.” The president has said campaign funds would be used to pay for the commercials going forward.

title: How the Supreme Court is reshaping the limits of religious rights in America
description: The Roberts court has redefined the separation of church and state. This term may show how far it will go.

title: Trump’s diesel deal with Russia shows how tied the prices are to Republican success this year
description: Trump has largely dismissed the focus on higher gas prices, but this deal with Russia suggests the president knows what’s at stake.

title: Trump’s midterm road show reveals GOP troubles — and his own priorities
description: Republicans need the president to mobilize voters, but his low approval ratings limit where he can help.

title: Democratic senator talks Trump's Russian diesel deal
description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks to Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire about President Trump's deal for Russian diesel and his claim of an "energy ceasefire" that did not materialize.

title: Republican strategist on how Trump's personal grievances could affect the GOP
description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Republican strategist Rina Shah about how President Trump's personal grievances and projects are affecting the chances of GOP candidates in the upcoming election.

title: Trump struggles to show voters he's focused on the cost of living
description: With a deal to import millions of tons of diesel fuel from Russia,  President Trump is struggling to show voters that he is focused on the cost of living ahead of the midterms.

title: Morning news brief
Texas' 15th Congressional District provides clues to state's Latino vote
description: The 15th Congressional District runs from the east of San Antonio all the way down into the Rio Grande Valley. This majority-Latino district provides a window into the Latino vote in Texas.

title: Takeaways from first S.C. Senate debate between Darline Graham, Annie Andrews
description: Sen. Darline Graham (R-South Carolina) clashed with Democrat Annie Andrews in their only scheduled debate of a Senate race that has become unexpectedly competitive.

title: Trump could face a new threat in January: A Democratic Senate
description: Republicans predict that Democrats will not confirm Supreme Court and Cabinet nominees if they retake the Senate in the midterm elections.

title: Abdul El-Sayed walks back Obama criticism ahead of their campaign event
description: The Michigan Democratic Senate nominee wrote an op-ed in 2012 expressing dismay at what he said were "failures' by Obama. In an NBC interview, El-Sayed blamed the comments on his youth.

title: Democrats are running on a scant agenda. Do they need more?
description: They lack a specific plan for governing, beyond turning back Trump and holding him accountable.

title: Arizona’s GOP keeps embracing election deniers who lose. It could happen again.
description: Alexander Kolodin made his political career by championing challenges to the 2020 results. Now he’s running to lead his state’s elections.

title: These are the voters who will decide the midterm elections
description: Move aside, “soccer moms.” Take our quiz to see which types of Americans will determine control of Congress in November.

title: 35 years ago today, Anita Hill testified before Congress
description: Hill’s testimony was a watershed in the conversation about workplace sexual harassment. The Almanac uses photo archives to understand where we are by examining where we’ve been.

title: Justice Department investigates TV networks, citing possible anti-trust violations
description: The move escalates Trump's fight with the press amid court battle over barring CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House.

title: Politics chat: Trump announces fuel deal with Russia. What does it mean for sanctions?
description: President Trump announced a deal to import Russian fuel to the U.S. We look at what this means for the sanctions he recently signed off on against Russia, as well as the U.S.'s support for Ukraine.

title: In one of the country's most competitive districts, a Democrat tries to keep her seat
description: In a highly competitive Washington congressional race, the incumbent Democrat has angered part of her party base and the Trump-backed Republican challenger faces backlash against the party in power.

title: Reshaped civil rights mission at Justice Department transforms its work, workforce
description: Harmeet Dhillon has pushed out hundreds of longtime attorneys, replaced many with inexperienced ideological allies, and used the division's enforcement powers to pursue the president's agenda.

title: DOJ investigating five TV networks over White House pool coverage
description: The agency said the probe seeks to determine whether Fox News, CNN, ABC, CBS and NBC violated antitrust laws. It marks a sharp escalation in the Trump administration’s use of its powers against perceived enemies in the press.

title: Trump suggests ‘Ocean of Americas’ as new name for Atlantic or Pacific
description: The president also floated the idea of naming an ocean after himself.

title: Trump says Ukraine should ‘get a new president’ after U.S.-Russia diesel deal
description: Ukraine’s Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world," Trump said Saturday, a day after praising Russia’s Putin.

title: Trump's economic strategy resemble similar policies in East Asia
description: Much of the Trump administration's economic policy has been inspired by successful industrial policies successful in East Asia, including those of competitor, China. Will those policies work in the U.S.?

title: Trump says he will ‘make a decision’ on Hegseth plan to live-stream execution
description: The Pentagon has said a firing squad for the Fort Hood shooter is scheduled for Dec. 3. “By showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did,” the president said.
